verses.1:
For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath. + 53:1 Mahalath is probably a musical or liturgical term; see also Psalm 88:1|PSA 88:1 . A Maskil + 53:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142. of David.
 The fool says in his heart,
 “There is no God.”
 They are corrupt; their ways are vile.
 There is no one who does good.
verses.2:
God looks down from heaven
 upon the sons of men
 to see if any understand,
 if any seek God.
verses.3:
All have turned away,
 they have together become corrupt; + 53:3 LXX worthless 
 there is no one who does good,
 not even one. + 53:3 Cited in Romans 3:10–12|ROM 3:10-12
verses.5:
There they are, overwhelmed with dread,
 where there was nothing to fear.
 For God has scattered the bones
 of those who besieged you.
 You put them to shame,
 for God has despised them.
verses.6:
Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion!
 When God restores His captive people, + 53:6 Or the fortunes of His people 
 let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!
